utterances.text: Yes, okay. Then please proceed. Mr. Emmerson, who is counsel for Mr. Haradinaj, will start his cross-examination. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Ms. Andjelkovic, I just want, if I may, to ask you for some points of clarification. You've been very careful in your evidence, if I may say so, to confine yourself to specific answers to specific questions, and so I want, if I may, to follow that and to ask you about specific, direct issues. First of all, can I get the chronology of your visits to Kosovo, and western Kosovo in particular, absolutely clear during this period of time? Can I just tell you what I think the position is and then seek your clarification as to whether I'm right or not. First of all, your first visit was -- or began on the 28th of February. You spent about a week in the Drenica region and then -- no?

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, actually, I arrived on the 28th of February, and if I remember correctly, it was a Sunday.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: So the next day, I went with a colleague to Drenica region --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- and I have to be perfectly honest and say that I had heard that there may have been an incident, but I wasn't at the point --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: At Likoshan?

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Cirez and Likoshane villages.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But at that point, I did not know exactly where I was going and what I was going to see there. So, you know, my involvement in that matter was really circumstantial and probably not very prudent.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: No. I'll come back to ask you a few questions about what you do know --

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- in respect of Qirez and Likoshan in a moment or two. But just to get the chronology right.

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So you arrive in Kosovo on about the 28th of February.

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And you make your way over towards the Decan region, western Kosovo, I think you said, about five or six days later; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I think within -- within that week that I was there, the beginning -- it was the first week of March.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: There's a period of days when you are in the Drenica region before you make your way over towards Peje and Decan.

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: One day only, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see. So, in fact, it would be pretty much at the beginning of March that you'd make your way over to western Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So, for example, on the 5th of March, the date of the Prekaz incident involving the Jashari family, you would already have been in the Decan area?

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I believe so.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Then I think you made a second visit at the end of March or the beginning of April?

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And that -- on that occasion you travelled to Decan and then to Ratishe.

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And I think you told us about how you travelled, and I'll come back to that in a moment. Now, we know from your reports that you were interviewing some people on the 9th of April.

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And you were also conducting interviews at the end of April?

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: But do we assume that you weren't in the region continuously, then, from the beginning of April to the end?

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir, I wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was going back and forth.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So do those different little cluster of interviews represent separate visits?

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, pretty much.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are some that are grouped and there are others that are on separate visits.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: It may not matter terribly much, but the group of interviews that took place on the 9th of April, do you know if you had been back to Prishtina or to Belgrade between the beginning of April and the 9th?

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would say yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You think yes?

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would -- I think yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Okay. That's very helpful. Now, going back then to the first visit. So -- I mean, I think you said a moment ago perhaps in retrospect it wasn't terribly prudent because you had heard about the Likoshan and Qirez incidents, and presumably you were moving into the Drenica area in the immediate aftermath of that?

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, that was before the funerals took place of the victims.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. I mean, did you come across Albanians during that period of time, while you were -- in the first day or two that you were in the Drenica regions?

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And did you manage to pick up from them any information about the level of tension in the Albanian community following those attacks?

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely. What I -- what I did see, there were long queues of people who were waiting to express their condolences to families who had lost members at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And I think you didn't investigate at Likoshan?

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: But there was somebody from the HLC who did. I'm not asking for a name, but there was somebody who did, wasn't there?

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was, yes. There was another --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Who actually went and spoke to the families and to the people in the area surrounding?

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And is that somebody that you were working with and had you travelled with that person?

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm, again, absolutely clear: I'm not going to ask for the name. In the collection of incident reports that you've seen, I mean there's actually a very easy way of working out which ones are yours and which ones are somebody else's, which is that they've got your initiates on them, haven't they, MA?

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And there are also the initials of the other person involved in the other reports?

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In the ones that were here, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. Now, you've expressed some concern about giving individuals' names, so I just want to be absolutely clear that we're talking about the right person. I don't want, obviously, to use their name in the light of what you've said. Would you be comfortable for me to use their initials, or does that raise the same considerations?

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you have any doubt, we can go into private session. It takes us two seconds and then you could give either initials or names.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you feel more comfortable, we'll do that immediately.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I would feel more comfortable --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm very happy --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: -- I don't know whether the person is a witness or not. You have to understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I entirely understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So I was asking you about that first --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I was asking you about that first visit. You told us that you met some Albanians and picked up a certain sense of information from them. But your colleague, who was an Albanian-speaking field-worker for the Humanitarian Law Centre, had conducted the HLC inquiry into the aftermath of Qirez and Likoshan?

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I mean, did you speak to one another about what you were respectively being told?

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Naturally enough.

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So you picked up, presumably, some of the information, albeit one removed, from her that she was being told about the state of tension and fear in the Albanian community in the light of those attacks?

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Again, just in broad terms, can you give us a sense of the reaction of the Albanian community immediately after those attacks in the area around where they occurred?

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. People were quite agitated, and as I said, there was a long queue in front of literally every -- every compound, because people wanted to express their condolences. Also, another person who was -- I can't say -- "host" is perhaps not the right word, but the person who was from the Council for the Defence of Human Rights and Freedoms from that area and who was actually taking us to these different households and families, he has warned me that it would be better if I didn't speak Serbian because people were very agitated, they were -- some were naturally quite -- quite frustrated because people had died, and so I didn't. So I kept quiet and I was just going around as this man was taking us.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: But you saw the villages?

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Just help us, if you can, about this: On -- in the "Spotlight" report - I don't ask you to turn it up at the moment - but in the "Spotlight" report there is a reference to an HLC researcher who toured the Ahmeti property on the 2nd of March and saw scrawled on the walls the words: "This is what will happen next time, too." Now, did you see those words on the walls? Do you remember?

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't recollect, really.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well. Very well. Now, generally, I think, although later on, you were investigating alleged crimes against Albanians as well --

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- initially, at this point in time, there was a division of function between you, was there not?

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, pretty much.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You were really tasked to concentrate on Serbs, Serb civilians?

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And your Albanian-speaking colleague was tasked to concentrate on Albanian victims of alleged crimes?

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, that was correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And obviously for us to get a full picture, then, of the sense of tension on both sides of the community, one would need to have some sense of what was being told not just to you but also to her?

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Both of you, then, would be filing your reports.

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And in some of the "Spotlight" reports, they're then brought together.

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And as we'll see in a little while, sometimes you're getting one account of an event --

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mmm.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- and she's getting a completely different account --

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- and the HLC will put the two together in a report and say, Well, this side says this or this group of people say that and they're in contradiction to one another?

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, pretty much.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. Now can I just ask you this, then: From your observations or from what people told you, at this time of heightened tension, after Likoshan, after Qirez, after Prekaz, even, can you confirm that really quite a large part of the community on both sides carried weapons, had weapons in their homes and carried weapons, hunting rifles and so on?

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would say yes because it was -- I'm from a city, and I was quite surprised how many people actually had hunting rifles.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I mean, we can see from your notes that really quite a lot of the Serbian people you spoke to had weapons in their homes.

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And so as these levels of tension were increasing, ordinary Albanian citizens had weapons and so did their Serb neighbours who they were living next door to?

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I suppose.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, I mean from your own --

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah. Those where it is mentioned, then I could say, Yes, people said they had. Did everyone have? I --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I can't ask you to make an assessment like that.

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: But from your own interviews, you found people who were saying, I have guns at my house and my neighbour, who is Albanian, has guns at his house?

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Did you have examples of them saying, My neighbour shot at me and I shot at him, shot back at him in one instance, I think?

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, it could be. I think so. I can't recall now.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'll take you that, if I may --

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure about neighbours --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- as an example.

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I don't want to confuse you.

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And to be fair, I'll take you --

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- to the specific examples I'm referring to from the passages that Mr. Re has already referred you to. Can I then come to the second visit at the end of March/the beginning of April.

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, you travelled, you've told us, to Ratishe and you've described a number of instances in which people told you about shooting incidents where there were no casualties and the people concerned, the people you spoke to, didn't generally know who was responsible because these things had happened at night.

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And against that background, can we just look at one or two of the examples that Mr. Re took you to. First of all - and for this I'm afraid we have to use the binder - could we look, please, first of all, at notebook 1, at page 32 to 33.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- I take it that we're dealing with the first section now, then. Perhaps ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is that in the first section, just after the cover page with a lot of names and then the first -- is that --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Because we have different -- that is where the ERN numbers are in grey?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. It's the one at the very bottom. It refers to "blue notebook, volume 1" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- and then some ERN numbers. That's the first major page section.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That will now already get a P number --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Because it was -- Madam Registrar, this, and I'll make that clear, this first section we find in the binder, which is notebook 1, draft translated, not in ERN sequential order but, as we understand from the Prosecution, the right chronological order of the original, that gets number ...?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be Exhibit Number P3, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, in order to avoid whatever confusion. At the bottom, it says: "Blue Notebook, Volume 1," not preceded by the name "Andjelkovic" as we find it in the third section --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- where it's preceded by the name. So that is clear. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: If you could just have a look at page 32, and this records your interviews that you were taken to by Mr. Re with the -- with Mr. and Mrs. Culafic --

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Culafic.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Culafic, I'm sorry. Do correct my pronunciation because I'm bound to make mistakes -- in Ratishe. And they described an incident to you that occurred at -- I just want to look. We see a passage beginning: "Wife," just immediately under the underlined words at the top of page 32. Do you have that? Yes.

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So that's -- you're speaking to Mrs. Culafic?

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is what she said.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. And then there's a passage beginning: "Nastadin," the following paragraph, which is, I think, is you speaking to her husband?

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is the husband.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And then over the page, at the bottom of page 33, the last paragraph is headed: "Wife," and that's again, I think, you speaking to the wife again?

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can I just ask you to read to yourself, looking back at page 32 at the first full paragraph, about halfway down, can you find the sentence in the middle of the paragraph: "My sons wanted to kill them ..." It's on page 32, first full paragraph --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Line 6.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- line 6, right in the middle of that first full paragraph: "My sons wanted to kill them."

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. Can you just -- just read to yourself the next three or four lines, down to the one -- the words: "He says it's his land." I think your finger has drafted a little further. Just down to where it says -- where she's referring to somebody who is claiming the land is his. Do you have that?

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And then if we just turn over the page to the other passage involving the wife there, a name is given. There's a reference to rocks being thrown at night, and then a name is given, Lulaj Zajma.

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: It says: "This was his land. We bought a hectare and 24 acres. We got the forest from the monarchy," and so on. Yes. What -- looking at those two passages together, what was Mrs. Culafic telling you about the person who had, she believed, was responsible for this attack?

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To be honest, sir, I'm not even sure that she was referring to the person --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see.

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- who was actually responsible for the attack. I think this was more general -- as I understood it at the time and as he says it, I think it was more in general, that this may have been somebody who had owned the land in the 1940s or--

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see.

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- I think that's what -- sometimes -- and, you know, and this just shows that I'm not a detective --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: No, no, and--

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- because I would ask immediately who --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm just trying to understand the significance of that to what they're describing, because she seems to be relating it in the passage that you've recorded to the incident that occurred, whether there was some long-standing problem between her and her neighbour.

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that what -- I'm not sure if I was clear yesterday or at any point today. I was there to record -- I would be going out in the field, and I was there to record what people said. I wasn't cross-checking --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, well that was -- I was going to come back to that. You're not there to investigate whether what they're telling you is the truth?

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, and I wasn't there to investigate who the person that is mentioned was or whether they had any troubles with neighbours over land.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: No. I --

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry to cause this confusion.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Not at all. Not at all. It's a matter of absolute clarification, in fact, that that was not part of your function when you were -- you were taking what people told you --

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- people who were upset --

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Pretty much.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- people who -- in a period of heightened tension on both sides, with a lot of people with guns, you were taking what people were saying to you at face value at that, perfectly properly, but reporting it back?

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. And then if we just turn over to page 38, the other -- the next passage, I think, that Mr. Re took you to, an interview with the family Delic. Do you have that? Just the top of page 38, on the 3rd of April.

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And I'll get the pronunciation of the village wrong if I say it before you do, so perhaps you could tell us exactly how to pronounce it.

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it's pronounced Lug Bunar.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Llug Bunar. And again, this is an example. This is a gentleman at his home who told you that he heard dogs outside, he heard a rush towards the orchard, he saw two men in the orchard. They fired, you've written, three or four shells; yes?

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: But then you say: "He took his hunting rifle and fired a shell in their direction."

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what he said.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: By the word "shell" -- I mean, it may be that there's a translation issue here, but do you mean bullets?

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it is a translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I recall, it was bullets rather than ...

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. And that was just an example I was giving you of -- where there had been an exchange of fire, people with a lot of weapons shooting at one another. And you say, I think, a little further down: "Shell casings were found." So I think it's clear we're talking about bullets?

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Bullets, yeah, I would say.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And a little further on, pages 39 and 40, Fatic, Radenko Fatic and some yarn. This was an interview where he told you in terms that it was his next-door neighbour.

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, he said it was his next-door neighbour.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And he told you that he had told his next-door neighbour that he saw him?

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and -- but he told me that he was not going to tell --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: He wasn't going to tell you the name. He told you that he didn't know if there was anybody other than his next-door neighbour involved.

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't recall that he said anyone else.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I think he told you that he didn't know whether it was --

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- there was anybody else. You see, just towards the bottom: "I don't know if there were more people. We only saw him." Very bottom of page 39, Ms. Andjelkovic. "I don't know if there were more people. We only saw him."

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And then you've recorded a name at the top of page 40 in that context, and I just wondered what the significance of that name, Sacir Bekir, is in that context?

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall, to be honest.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can I ask you: Might it be that the found out the name of the neighbour from somebody else?

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't say -- I mean, I would really have to look at the notes and see exactly where it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: It might, in fact, be helpful if you did that for us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Yes. Why don't we do it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can't promise you that I will recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: No, of course. Of course. I'm not -- I wouldn't expect it for a moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you have a copy of the notes with you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Of course I don't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then I think they are on e-court, under P1, I think it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: We have the ERN number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Would it be the most efficient use of time if I continued to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, and let the registrar find the document meanwhile --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- cross-examine, we try to find the passage that's the equivalent --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: The next page, 210.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Because it's very, very close to the end of that first notebook. It's within the last couple of pages of the notebook.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I mean, it may be that you can find it yourself, can you? Do you have it there, no?

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, this is a translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Fine. Let's see if we can find it for you and come back to that question. Can I then ask you about the inquiries that were going on whilst you were speaking to these people, the inquiries that were being conducted by your Albanian-speaking colleague. Just let me put something to you, because we have the report so it's not difficult to piece the chronology together. So I think while you were conducting those inquiries, she was collecting statements from villagers in Gllogjan about the police operation that had been mounted there on the 24th of March. That's right, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I think you weren't there in Gllogjan --

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- but she was and that's what she was doing.

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I think we'll see in due course that there are very many more statements in the HLC's possession from Albanians who were - if I can use this term loosely - victims of the police operation on the 24th of March than the rather small number of statements you took from the Stojanovic family members?

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I believe so.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: There were 28 or so statements considered by the HLC in all in preparing "Spotlight" report 26 that we've looked at?

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember the exact number.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, it's remembered to in the report, so if I'm wrong, I'm sure I'll be corrected. I think she was working really from a much earlier stage --

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- on the 24th of March investigation than you were?

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And presumably, though, on your journey --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- may I remind you of one thing --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- We were taught during the lessons we followed, both of us, that if you're speaking the same language, that you should make a pause between answer and question.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So presumably, whilst you were travelling back together to Prishtina, you would have discussed with her what the products of her inquiry was?

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was a bit later actually when we filed reports, not immediately.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well. But over the period of time that you were working with your Albanian-speaking colleague, you would have picked up from her, broadly speaking, what it was she was filing reports about in relation to the 24th of March?

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And, again, I don't want to take you in detail to the "Spotlight" report, but could we just very quickly look at the passage that deals with this.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: It's -- so we're now -- need a new P number for the section at the end of this bundle which contains the two "Spotlight" reports?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Perhaps we'll do it in the order in which they were presented.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That means we first go to the second section with this draft translation, second notebook, ERN number sequential. That would be -- Madam Registrar, would be ...?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this would be Exhibit Number P4, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And then we have the next one, a series of translations, or at least English versions of incident reports ranging from e20glodj.doc numbering down to e2glodj.doc and then followed by e23glodj.doc, e22glodg.doc, and e21glodj.doc. That series would have what number, Madam Registrar?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the incident reports would have Exhibit Number P5, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Then we now come to the relevant section, that is two "Spotlight" reports numbered 26 and 27, in English; 26, pages 1 to 24, ERN numbers 00649667 and then numbering upwards, up to and including 690, last three digits; and "Spotlight" report 27, pages 1 to 24, ERN numbers K0078701 up to 713, the ERN numbers usually containing two -- two printed pages under one ERN number. So, therefore, we're now referring to these -- Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, these two "Spotlight" reports will be P6, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So you're referring to P6. Mr. Emmerson, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And I think, if it helps to have them on the screen at the same time, the relevant report --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I don't know whether they have been uploaded already.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: We've uploaded them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You've uploaded them?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay, fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So it's document identification 1D978 at page 11. I'm sorry, page -- 1D988. I apologise. So document 1D978 at 1D988. And if we can just zoom in on the paragraph beneath the heading there, beneath the -- I'm sorry, we're on the wrong page. No -- that's fine. That's fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Looking at the references to the 24th of March itself there, we can see the statements - this is the second paragraph - made to HLC researchers by 28 witnesses; yes?

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Suggested that on the 24th of March, Serbian police officers killed in flight three Kosovar Albanians, shelled houses in which unarmed civilians had taken cover, placed in jeopardy the lives of children, women, and arrested persons in order to defend themselves, and used the house of the only non-Albanian family as a military facility." Yes? Do you know who they're referring to when they say there, "the house of the only non-Albanian family there was used as a military facility"?

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The only house that this may be is the house of family Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Stojanovic?

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. And if we just go to the following page, I think what we can see, just going up a little --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could speakers please slow down.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: We see in the second paragraph there reference to the accounts given to your Albanian-speaking colleague, I think; yes?

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hmm, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And in the third paragraph there, reference to the account given by the witnesses you spoke to.

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And then in the fourth paragraph, a statement by the Serbian ministry 1 of Internal Affairs; yes?

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So all of that material, contradictory material, I think, in terms of how the incident began was before the HLC in the preparation of this report and put together in that way?

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right. But, again, I have to say the summary reports like this would usually be based on the interviews that people like me did in the field --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- for better or for worse, and then they would be put together with different other information --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- that was available by people who were lawyers at the HLC.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: So they would then put a report and publish it.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well. That's very helpful. Rather than go through the headings on the screen, in this particular instance, it's probably just easier if we turn the pages in the bundle to see the headings there, between pages 11 through to 16. And can I deal with it generically in this way: What people who had made statements to your Albanian-speaking colleague were saying - and we have the reports but without taking time to go through them all - essentially came down to this, I think: First of all, that police began by firing on two men. That was the account, by and large, that was being given by the Albanian witnesses that your Albanian-speaking colleague spoke to; yes?

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall, really. I would have to read the reports again.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well. In that case, I'm not going to -- I'm not going to press you. We can read the summary for ourselves. I'm not going to press you in that case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, just for the record, since we relied on P6, it is the report number 26 you were referring to.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Because there are two reports.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: There are two reports.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can you help me about this: From what your Albanian-speaking colleague told you, did you understand that there was a general perception in the village that this was -- this had been a major assault on the town, on the village of Gllogjan?

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the interview that she did?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I recall, I think it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. And do you recall her mentioning to you that there were allegations that Serb forces went on a rampage in the village?

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Rampage? Maybe that would be too strong a word at that stage.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see.

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And I don't recall that anyone exactly described it like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: But there were allegations, weren't there, of a group of teenagers, either three or four, being shot as they were running away?

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that was -- that was what came out from --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Of Serb military helicopters firing on civilians from the air -- well, if it's not something you remember, just say so. It's in the report. We can look at it --

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I remind both of you. Apart from the speed of your speech, it seems that you're now and then, if you're satisfied with the answer, you already speak at the same time when the witness has not fully completed. You also, if there seems to be some understanding, you interrupt. If people are speaking at the same time, our court reporters are totally unable to record that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And there were allegations that quite large numbers of people were arrested and ill-treated by the Serb police immediately afterwards, I think?

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That, I remember. That, I remember from -- from the reports and from what my colleagues were saying, that there was a fairly large group of people were rounded up at first.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And that school children were used by the Serb forces as a human shield?

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know there was something about a school, but I really --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I mean, again, we can see that -- the passage in the report. And that houses in the village were shelled?

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Shelled? What do you mean when you say "shelled"?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, that they were attacked with heavy weapons and inside the village of Gllogjan.

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot recall heavy weapons. I do recall that there was fighting and there was -- that there was another -- that police sent reinforcements.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But I really can't recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: For present purposes, that's all I need to ask you about that. I'll come back to its relevance, if I may, to some of your other inquiries, in a few moments.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I have to remind both of you, I wouldn't say bad habits, but at least it's difficult to control this. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Coming back now, then, to the 9th of April visit, to the interviews you conducted on the 9th of April, I think you've told us that on that occasion you travelled to Gjakova by bus from Prishtina; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes?

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I went to Gjakova.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And what route would the bus take you to Gjakova?

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Actually, I have to -- I would have to say that I don't recall exactly whether I went on a direct bus or I went via Peje, because that was another --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- that was another option.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So you could have gone Peje?

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I could have gone Prishtina, Peje, and then changed in Peje to Gjakova.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Which would be -- which would take you along the main road --

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, main road.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- and through Decani?

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Through Decani, definitely.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And, actually, I'm not -- now I can't tell whether it was --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- that I went all the way to Gjakova or I got out in Decan, because there were interviews that I conducted in Decan.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Okay. But certainly you saw no evidence along the road of it being closed by the KLA?

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And you then, on that occasion, the 9th of April occasion, conducted your interviews with Vladimir Stojanovic and his mother - and again if I've got my pronunciation wrong, tell me - Ljubica?

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ljubica.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Ljubica.

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And that was when you received an account of how the incident began that was --

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- in conflict with the account that had been given to you -- given to the HLC through your Albanian-speaking colleague?

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, can we look briefly at the -- at the record that you filed for the interview with Vladimir Stojanovic. And we can have it on the screen as a doc. -- Defence doc. ID 1D1255. We have it in the file as e4glodj.doc. E4glodj.doc. And if we can just --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And that's part of P5.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: First of all, these glodj.doc numbers, they weren't presumably put on by you and your Albanian-speaking colleague?

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: They were put on by the HLC, which explains why they don't run in sequence for you.

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. And this was an interview, we can see - I don't ask to turn it over on the screen at the moment - but we can see in the paper version, this was an interview conducted on the 9th of April, the report was filed on the 9th of April, and it related to an incident which is recorded there as the 14th of September, 1997. Now, I know what you're going to say. You dealt with two things in this statement. You dealt with something that had happened in September 1997, and you also dealt with the events of the 24th of March.

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, I want to ask you about the 24th of March passage.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Could we look at the second page where the body of the statement is set out, which is 1256.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can you see the third paragraph, beginning "We called Decan on the radio ..."

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: " ... on the radio-phone we have in the house, but they had already been informed about what was going on." Yes?

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: In short, the allegation that Vladimir Stojanovic was making was that the police were fired on first; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And the allegation that was being made by the Albanian side of the community was that the police had fired on two men, and that is how the incident had begun?

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. If we just look through that first passage, "We called Decan on the radio-phone we have in the house but they had already been informed about what was going on." There's a reference then at 10.30 a.m. to "those in the neighbour's house" firing rockets. "The shooting lasted for 15 minutes. Then the police arrived and came into our yard from where they opened fire at the Haradinaj house."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, when reading, speed goes up always. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You can see that passage?

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Stojanovic was telling you that the police were shooting at the Haradinaj compound from his property?

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I understood, and if I recall when I talked to him, he claimed that they were in the house, and I think his mother said something similar, that they -- when they heard shooting first, he ushered them all into their house --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- and then the police came into the yard.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And it's very close to the Haradinaj family compound, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That seems to be, but I can't say but I haven't been --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And you've never been there because you interviewed them -- you interviewed them in Decan?

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was in Decan when I interviewed him.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So one thing he was clearly telling you, though, is that police forces were firing on the Haradinaj compound from his property; yes?

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is -- that is what he says, and that -- what he said at the time, that is, according to -- to the record.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. Now, he told you about a rocket being fired out from the Haradinaj compound towards the police, I think; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, that's what it says here.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Did he tell you that the police were firing rockets into the Haradinaj compound, or is that something that he left out of his account?

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I -- I don't recall that, because I would have certainly noted that. Most of the things, again, I have to say, I noted verbatim.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. So if he left that -- if that's not in your notes, it's because he deliberately chose not to tell you about that.

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That -- that would probably be the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. And then there's a reference a little further down to the fact that there was a helicopter overhead. Do you see that? It's the -- yes? Towards the bottom of that main paragraph on the screen?

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Going back to the reference to a radio-telephone, can I ask you this: Do you know what somebody meant by radio-telephone?

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Did you understand what he meant by radio-telephone?

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't -- I'm not sure. I'm not sure I did. I'm not sure whether -- what sort of phone that was, whether that was a radio or -- I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. I mean, if it was a radio, I mean, were radios, as far as you could observe, in common usage in western Kosovo for civilians?

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't know, sir. I haven't been to that many houses.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can I ask you --

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those houses.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- did this gentleman or his mother tell you one way or the other whether any members of the family worked for the police?

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there was -- one of the brothers was with the police force, I understood, in Gjakova. I think it was in Gjakova. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. And, again, can you confirm this, that when you interviewed Mrs. Stojanovic, one of the things that she was keen to tell you is that the perception in the village and in the newspapers that she and the Stojanovics had been regularly informing on the Haradinaj family to the police wasn't true?

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, could you ...

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Let's take it -- I'll break the question down into stages.

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Do you recall being told by Mrs. Stojanovic that there were reports, including newspaper reports, that their property was being used by the police as a place from which to maintain observations on the Haradinaj family compound and provide information?

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I could --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely, please turn to the report.

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I could turn --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: It's immediately afterwards. If you look at the last paragraph on page 2. It's obviously a summary, but just five lines up: "The newspapers wrote that the first shots came from my house and that I told the police about what is going on in the village," and she denies that?

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I mean, either from the Stojanovics or from the inquiries that you made through your -- or your Albanian colleague made, did you come to understand that there was a view commonly held in the village that the Stojanovics had or were, in part, responsible for that assault on the village?

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot really -- I cannot make judgement one way or another.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What Mrs. Stojanovic told me was that -- what she said was there was that perception, but she had also claimed that she had fairly good relations with her neighbours --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- for years.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'll make it up to you that I'm certainly not asking you to comment on whether it was the truth or not. You can't possibly do that. But she did tell you, I think you've just confirmed, that there was a perception --

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- that the Stojanovic home had been a place from which information was provided to the police and then the position from which the assault was first launched on the Haradinaj compound, that that was a perception?

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are we talking in general or are we talking about a single incident? I'm not now quite clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, again it's my fault completely for putting too long a question, and I'll break it into stages. You've confirmed, I think, a moment ago, you said to me, "that was the perception."

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, the perception was, as I understand it - correct me if I've got this wrong - the perception was that the Stojanovic house had been used by the police as a place from which to observe the Haradinaj family -- the Haradinaj family compound, first of all.

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From -- from her statement --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- that appears to be. But I cannot say whether it was my perception.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And secondly, it is true, according to them, that their house was, in fact, used to launch the assault on the Haradinaj compound, because the police officers were firing, as you just told us a moment ago, according to Mr. Stojanovic, on the Haradinaj compound from their property.

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, from their property.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: From their property?

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure about the house --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- but from their property.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And you've told us one member of the family was in the police, and I just want to ask you again: The radio-telephone, did you understand that to have been something that had been specially provided to the Stojanovics; and if so, by whom?

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really can't answer that because I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Finally this, on this statement: I think it's right that Vladimir Stojanovic told you - this is the second-to-last paragraph on the first page of the statement, the main text, beginning "After the clash ..." - Mr. Stojanovic, Vladimir, told you that immediately afterwards at least, the family were going back on a daily basis?

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is what they said.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Of course, during that time quite a lot of people in the village had evacuated, hadn't they, in Gllogjan, after the 24th of March; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Actually, I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You don't think so.

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a month later, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, we'll come to -- that's not an issue I'm going to ask you about, the end of May. But you don't think people left Gllogjan on the 24th of March, when the police attacked the village?

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh. Left Glodjane?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Who? I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: The Albanian community of Gllogjan.

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They -- they were displaced, I understood, at the time, but -- but I can't say where because I didn't interview people at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Mrs. Stojanovic, she told you, I think --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, I seek one clarification.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You just said "They were displaced, I understood, at the time ..." What did you exactly mean? Because Mr. Emmerson was earlier referring to a specific date, which was the 24th of March.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did you tell us that they were displaced already prior to that, or on that day, or that -- it's not entirely clear to me.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I'm sorry if I haven't been clear, because this is, A --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Please don't apologise.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: -- years ago, and then, B, there were a lot throughout the period, so that may, you know, affect what and how I answer, and I apologise because I've never done this before. There were times when people would be displaced because there was shooting and there was an incident, and then when things calmed down, they would come back. That was the pattern for quite a few months in Kosovo overall.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And I think what you're confirming is that, following the police assault on the village of Gllogjan, quite a lot of the Albanian community left and were displaced for a time.

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I seem to remember that that was the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to -- to the reports of my colleagues.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, yes. And Mrs. Stojanovic, Ljubica Stojanovic, could we just look very briefly at her witness statement again, or the report you filed for her.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: This is Defence doc. identification D11252 at 1253. Just one point I wanted to ask you about there.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: If one looks at the passage three lines down from the top. Sorry, it's not quite loaded yet. Do you have the paper copy?

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. Whilst it's loading, perhaps I can ask you some questions from the paper copy. Mr. Re asked you about a group of men who she told you had stopped her son Dragoslav - so it's the following page, please. Following page; lovely, thank you very much. I'm in the first paragraph, third line down. She told you that her son Dragoslav had been stopped at the end of February by a group of men who were armed and who took his pistol and then gave it back to him?

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And I think she told you that after searching him, they made him sign a piece of paper saying that they'd given the gun back; yes?

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Did she tell you whether any of the other male members of the family carried guns?

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I don't recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I want to move on now, if I may, to the end of April, and you were asked about that visit and some of the statements that you made on the 20th of April, or around about the time of that -- of that visit. Could I ask you to look, please, in your diary.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And this will be P3, that's notebook 1, and I could be wrong about that, in fact. I'm sorry. No, it's not, it's P4, notebook 2, at page 15.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, you were asked about an elderly gentleman who you said had told you that he was detained in Gllogjan; yes?

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I just want to look at what you recorded in your notebook. This is at page 15, just a bit below halfway. "What is going on now, you know better. I dropped my something. If I did something wrong, where are your sons to fight? We would like to have a free village. They released us." "They urgently released us," is what the translation says, what that is a reference to. And for me this is the second one. Then he said this: "They didn't do anything to the women. They said they would not do anything to the elderly. They transferred us to Irzniq by tractor. We would meet patrols every 200 metres, but they didn't say anything to us. This happened on Wednesday. My son went to the village for me. They did not hit me." Yes?

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So those were your notes as to what he was telling you at that time.

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what -- what the old man, Mr. Stijovic, told me at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I just wanted to ask you very briefly, if I could, about how that then comes into the incident report, because we can see -- I mean, you've made a very clear statement there that, first of all, that they didn't hit him.

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is not my statement, sir. It is the note of the statement of Mr. Stijovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: A very clear record of his statement to you --

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- that he was not hit?

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And that he was given reassurance, in effect?

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: If we could just look very briefly at the equivalent report that you filed, which is -- just bear with me one moment. It's e19glodj, which is not in the system, which is why I don't have a Defence identification for it because it was one of the documents served for the first time in that form, I think, last night. Can I just ask you about this: This is an interview that's recorded as having taken place on the 25th of April in respect of an incident on the 22nd of April, filed as a report on the 27th of April. If we could just look at the second page --

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you would --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Do you have it?

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- please tell me -- I have it, I'm sure. But what am I looking at?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry, you're looking in that part of the bundle that contains your incident reports, and you're looking at e19glodj.doc, which is the equivalent passage to your -- the passage of your notes that we've just looked at. And if we just look three paragraphs down, we see that the passage that we've just -- or something -- something equivalent to the passage we've just looked at. I just wanted to check this: In terms of the possibility of errors creeping in from time to time, in the second paragraph, do you see the reference, about halfway down, "They hit me on the head a few times"?

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "And my cap fell off."

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. Do you understand how that --

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, okay, I understand -- I'm not sure I understand how, because you have to understand, this is a translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The filed reports are a translation of the reports, and I have -- really, I had no access to my reports once they were filed. I mean, I did have access, but this was in 1998. He used a very peculiar word to say that his cap fell, and I do remember because it was such a peculiar word, I remember it would -- literally it would say "they injured my cap a little bit." This is why I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you for the clarification.

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: On this same visit, you interviewed Mijat Stojanovic [sic].

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And if we can have a look at Defence doc. identification 1D1008, and we have it in the paper copy as eglodj -- e10glodj.doc. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, I just want you to pause for a moment because you gave us some evidence yesterday which I want to try to clarify with you, because we obviously have not got all your incident reports, but do we have all your notebooks, as far as you can tell?

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know, really.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well. Very well. But you thought at one point, you said you thought you might have interviewed the cousin in relation to this incident and you might have interviewed Dragoslav some time much later on?

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I just want to ask you about this interview. This is the only one for which we have a record, which is both in your notebook and in the incident report that you've filed.

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You said yesterday that the first time you heard the name Haradinaj was in connection with this incident where the two Stojanovic brothers and their cousin had been taken from a house to another house and beaten and questioned, and that a man by the name of Haradinaj, who seemed to be in authority, was coming in and out of the room?

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That was the first time that I heard the name.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So that would be this report, because this was the first one?

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. So just so that we're clear, because at least we know now what the precise source of that comment was; yes?

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And if we could just look, please. You've listed in the incident report the victim identification on the first page, Mijat Stojanovic, the person making the statement to you, Dragoslav Stojanovic, and Veselin Stojanovic; yes?

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they would -- they were the --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Stijovic, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- that travelled. Stijovic, yeah. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And then you've listed alleged perpetrator information. Nasim Haradinaj; yes?

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Just pause for a moment. Over the page, Nemonaj, I can't read what that's supposed to say, but somebody called Nemonaj; yes?

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And then unidentified Liberation Army of Kosova members; yes?

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, if we can just drop down in the body of the statement a little bit to look at the second and third main paragraphs on the first page, where the account is related, if we just -- if we can just pick up about seven or eight lines up from the bottom, can you see a sentence beginning "When Nasim Haradinaj came in ..."

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: "When Nasim Haradinaj came in, the beatings stopped. He said to them not to beat us, but they went on anyway." Yes?

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And a little further down, the following paragraph: "They took us upstairs. We laid down on the concrete floor. Nasim ordered us to get up. They offered us cigarettes and coffee"; yes?"

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: "Nasim said they weren't allowed to beat us."

utterances.speaker: MARIJANA ANDJELKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. And then over the page, if we can just look at the second page for a moment, third paragraph down begins: "Then Nasim turned up again and said they were letting us go because I'm a Montenegrin." Do you have that? Third paragraph on the second page, first sentence. It begins -- it's on the screen in front of you, if that's easier.
